Tlokwe Toilets

By: Phakamile Hlubi | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Local councillors in Potchefstroom in the North West are outraged at the erection of hundreds of toilets on vacant land, when people in surrounding areas have little or no sanitation services.

Unique Selling Point:
Some opposition councillors in the Tlokwe municipality are calling for the immediate removal of Tlokwe housing manager, Lawson Mohlomi. They believe his irregular appointment is partly to blame for some of the housing problems they have in the area. Mohlomi was re-appointed as manager of housing and planning since 2013 despite opposition from opposition parties. The reason his re-appointment caused a stir was because his appointment was deemed irregular because he does not have the minimum qualifications to fulfil the duties.

Summary:
Furthermore, the former MEC for local government and housing in the North West, (now ANCYL president) Collen Maine sent a letter to the municipality saying "his appointment was irregular and is not endorsed".


A report which was tabled before council in August this year stated that "If council does not rescind the decision to appoint Mohlomi, the MEC will issue a declamatory order". It also states that his appointment was made without a formal report being served at the council. He was also not recommended by the interviewing panel as a suitable candidate to take up the job.

Some of the housing problems faced by the municipality include a failed RDP housing project in Sonderwater. According to a report by the NHBRC over five hundred houses were built with poor workmanship. In a report which was issued in 2011 the NHBRC finds that remedial action must be taken to repair or rebuild these houses. The estimated cost at that time to repair the damage was over 18 million rand.

We will shoot an interview with a case study in Sonderwater. This interview will demonstrate the suffering experienced by the residents as a result of this project. Also the councillors claim that no action has been taken to remedy the situation as recommended by the report.

Greenfields - We will interview David Kham in Geenfields. He is one of the independent councillors serving in the municipality. David is also a former ANC councillor who was expelled, along with several other councillors in the area for voting with the opposition to remove ANC appointed mayor Maphetle Maphetle in 2013. (It's worth mentioning that Kham and Moolman spearheaded the Constitutional court application which resulted in by-election results in Tlokwe being set aside because of vote rigging).

In Greenfields there are dozens of incomplete houses or foundations as a result of a contractor who began some of the construction, and then he ran off with the money and never completed the project.


Further information:
There is also a new housing project that has tongues wagging in the area. The erection of about a thousand toilets on a vacant piece of land along the N12 in Extension 9. The municipality has simply erected toilets, not housing units or structures. The toilets were erected just before the elections. Councillors claim this project was not endorsed by the council and they have questioned the process.

We get a response from Mr Mohlomi himself about the allegations levelled against him. We also chat to the mayor, Kgotso Khumalo too respond to the issue of Mohlomi's 'irregular appointment', as well as how to address some of the housing problems faced by the community.
We also interview the current MEC for local government in the North West to find out how they will resolve the impasse. Especially if it seems the municipality is determined to retain him.

Press Release:


Tlokwe Toilets
How did hundreds of toilets mysteriously appear on vacant land next to the N12 near Potchefstroom while residents are living in RDP homes unfit for human habitation? Carte Blanche sheds light on a litany of housing problems in the North West municipality of Tlokwe


Script:


TLOKWE TOILETS
JOYCE SEELE Sonderwater Resident (SUBTITLE) (0094N7 1:29 seconds in): “When they came to tell us that the land is ready for them to build on, I was overjoyed because I’d been living in a shack for the last 18 years.”
Joyce Seele spent her entire life living in an informal settlement, and never thought she would ever live in a proper house.
She was one of hundreds of residents of the Tlokwe Municipality in Potchefstroom in the North West, who received houses as part of the Sonderwater Project in 2011.
But her happiness was short lived.
JOYCE SEELE, Sonderwater Resident 00951H 01:55 “Living in this house with raw sewage in the yard, it’s not the kind of life which is fit for human beings, especially when you have children
The plumbing infrastructure is so poorly laid out that raw sewage flows directly into her back yard creating a health risk for her and her family.
VIZ OF JOYCE AND SPADE
Sello Tshoaedi is another beneficiary of the project.
After years on the waiting list, the 59 year old was given a house with a bath…but no taps VIZ OF BATH WITH NO TAPS
SELLO TSHOAEDI, Sonderwater Resident (0025O0 16 seconds in) SUBTITLE: “Ha ke batla.. When I want to take a bath I have to take water from the sink and pour it into the bath. (OLAY WITH VIZ OF HIM & NAT SOUND POURING WATER)
And the house has no ceiling EXPOSED CEILING SHOT
David Kham was an ANC councillor in 2011. He was aware of some of the problems with the project. DAVID CUTAWAY WITH WOMAN
(BONGANI BINGWA 0033P3 IS THE SOUND OK, WIND!): “Let’s talk about housing. Behind you there appears to be what looks like a foundation. What is going on here?”
DAVID KHAM, Independent Tlokwe Councillor (0023H7 2:15):“This project was intended to create comfort and security for our people in the form of housing. But Officials who are corrupt colluded with contractors on this project.”
These slabs of concrete dotted all over Sonderwater are in fact dozens of foundations of incomplete houses which contractors were paid for. WIDE VIZ FOUNDATIONS & HOUSES
BONGANI PTC: “So shoddy was the workmanship on the house in the corner, it had to be demolished because it wasn’t fit for human habitation. Next door they are rebuilding their house at their own expense, and their neighbours, well they’ve simply erected a shack on the foundation”
An investigation by national building regulator, the NHBRC in April of that year, found that out of the six hundred and eighty five (685) houses built in the duration of the under the Project, five hundred and fifty six (556) didn’t meet the most basic building standards. WIDE SHOT HOUSES AND THEN OLAY OLAY WITH CLOSE UP VIZ OF POOR WORKMANSHIP; ROOF ETC.

BONGANI PTC: "In just a few steps I've already covered most of what was to be built on this foundation. See even if the Tlokwe housing project had delivered according to specifications, whatever structure was going to be built here could hardly be described as giving dignity to it's inhabitants"
Meanwhile, about 5 kilometers away, hundreds of brick toilets which were built on vacant land in Ikageng near the N12 freeway have caused a stir
WIDE SHOT BRICK TOILETS
The toilets are not operational because the infrastructure for the sewage pipelines has not yet been built. MORE VIZ TOILETS
BONGANI PTC: "It's the perfect example of a white elephant project and it's quite astounding. Toilets in an open veld extending all the way to the highway. It's meant to be the foundation of a housing project, but at this stage, it's an open invitation for squatting."
Councillors say the project, which so far has cost 12 million rands, wasn’t approved and hasn’t been budgeted for. VIZ TOILES
HJ Moolman a local councillor, says this project is just another example of dubious decision making on the part of the senior housing manager. HJ CUTAWAY
HJ MOOLMAN, DA Councillor, Tlokwe (0013WM 00:25 seconds) “Why not build a house with the toilet? Why do you only build a toilet? This is an issue of dignity, it’s an issue of safety
Whilst in surrounding areas like the Marikana informal settlement, residents survive with little or no basic sanitation services.. VIZ MARIKANA SHACKS
SHOTS OF MARIKANA INFOMAL SETTLEMENT
BONGANI BINGWA (0020VV 00:59 seconds): “So hang on, we’ve got communities here where a number of houses are sharing one toilet, and yet there’s a number of toilets in a vacant field?” OLAY MARIKANA SHACKS INTO BONGANI’S BITE
JOHANNES JOHNSON, Former Councillor, Tlokwe (0006L5): “We can’t allow anymore of our municipality’s to be run as if they are tuckshops. People are sitting, like you are seeing here. They are in need of developments.”
Johannes Johnson is another former ANC councillor. He and David Kham were part of a group of ANC members who were expelled from the party. CUTAWAY SPLIT SCREEN KHAM AND JOHNSON SIDE BY SIDE FREEZE
In 2013 the pair rebelled against the ANC and voted with the opposition to remove the former mayor, Maphetle Maphetle, allegedly because of corruption.
An act which resulted in their expulsion.
With the help of attorney HJ Moolman, the same councillors won a landmark Constitutional Court judgement against the IEC over election irregularities in the Tlokwe by-elections of 2013.
Now they are teaming up again to go back to court over the appointment of the senior manager of human settlements, Lawson Mohlomi.
JOHANNES JOHNSON, Former Councillor, Tlokwe 0006L5: “05:40 “This manager is not fit. He cost council a lot of money, and that money must be recovered.
Lawson Mohlomi has been the senior manager of housing and planning in the municipality since 2007.
Yet, despite Mohlomi’s lengthy service to the Municipality, Moolman believes the failed Sonderwater housing project is further evidence that he is not equipped for the position.
HJ MOOLMAN, DA Councillor, Tlokwe (000103 07:28) “He was never recommended by the panel, and two he did not possess the minimum qualifications for that specific management post”
During our investigation, we came across Mohlomi’s Linked In profile in which he claims to have a degree in Commerce from Wits University.
WIDE LINKD IN PROFILE & THEN CLOSE UP & ZOOM IN ON B COMMERCE CLAIM
We approached Wits to verify this claim and their response was that nobody with that name has graduated with a degree from the institution. (INSERT EMAIL FROM WITS UNIVERSITY OR CB VIZ OF WITS
Meanwhile, Johnson was so outraged over Mohlomi’s irregular appointment that for over a year he wrote letters to the municipality and the department of co-operative governance questioning the decision. (DISPLAY TWO LETTERS; USE FLASH NAT SOUND)
JOHANNES JOHNSON Former Councillor, Tlokwe (00042A 04:44): “I even went so far as to report this matter to the province to the MEC’s office with the Director General, but nothing came up
Finally in June 2015, the current ANC Youth League president, Collen Maine, who, at that time, was the MEC of Local Government in the North West, ordered the municipality to remove Mohlomi immediately, because his appointment was irregular and didn’t follow process.
HJ MOOLMAN, DA Councillor (0001O3 13:48): “Since the MEC wrote to the mayor more than a year ago, each and every month his salary was authorized by this administration, including the municipal manager. How can you do that if you know that in your right mind this person was unlawfully appointed?”
But despite this, in a council meeting this week, the majority ANC led council voted for Mohlomi to stay in his position.
HJ MOOLMAN, DA Councillor (0001O3 04:58): “Why didn’t they pursue the contractor? Why has nothing been done and why hasn’t the report been tabled before council?

We tracked down KRM Consulting, the Project Managers and contractors of the Housing Project to get their side of the story.
Despite numerous attempts on our part the, the Executive Director, Kemiso Khumoeng chose not respond to our questions or a request for an interview.
BONGANI PTC (0036RD): “So were the toilets built just before the local government elections just a ploy to get votes? What about the defective workmanship on so many of those houses? And of course the burning issue of the underqualified Mr. Mohlomi? These were some of the burning issues we wanted to put to the mayor. And having agreed to and promised an on camera interview, he cancelled at the last minute”
Back in Sonderwater, all Joyce wants is to live a dignified life with her family
JOYCE SEELE, Sonderwater resident, (0103C3 20 seconds in): “I want the council to fix the house. So that when I die, my children can inherit a proper home.”

PROMOS
(VO) 15 SECONDS
Carte Blanche exposes a controversial housing project in the municipality of Tlokwe in Potchefstroom in the North West. Could the appointment of an unqualified housing manager be to blame?
JOHANNES JOHNSON, Former Councillor, Tlokwe (0006L5): We can’t allow anymore of our municipality’s to be run as if they are tuckshops.
(VO) 15 SECONDS
Councillors in the Tlokwe municipality of Potchefstroom in the North West are outraged at the construction of toilets in a vacant field, when residents in nearby areas have little or no sanitation services
HJ MOOLMAN, DA Councillor, Tlokwe (0013WM 00:25 seconds) “Why not build a house with the toilet? Why do you only build a toilet? This is an issue of dignity”

(VO) 10 SECONDS
DAVID KHAM, Independent Tlokwe Councillor (0023H7 2:15):“This project was intended to create comfort and security for our people in the form of housing. But Officials who are corrupt colluded with contractors on this project.”

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Local councillors in Potchefstroom in the North West are outraged at the erection of hundreds of toilets on vacant land, when people in surrounding areas have little or no sanitation services.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Some opposition councillors in the Tlokwe municipality are calling for the immediate removal of Tlokwe housing manager, Lawson Mohlomi. They believe his irregular appointment is partly to blame for some of the housing problems they have in the area. Mohlomi was re-appointed as manager of housing and planning since 2013 despite opposition from opposition parties. The reason his re-appointment caused a stir was because his appointment was deemed irregular because he does not have the minimum qualifications to fulfil the duties.
metadata.Summary: Furthermore, the former MEC for local government and housing in the North West, (now ANCYL president) Collen Maine sent a letter to the municipality saying "his appointment was irregular and is not endorsed". A report which was tabled before council in August this year stated that "If council does not rescind the decision to appoint Mohlomi, the MEC will issue a declamatory order". It also states that his appointment was made without a formal report being served at the council. He was also not recommended by the interviewing panel as a suitable candidate to take up the job. Some of the housing problems faced by the municipality include a failed RDP housing project in Sonderwater. According to a report by the NHBRC over five hundred houses were built with poor workmanship. In a report which was issued in 2011 the NHBRC finds that remedial action must be taken to repair or rebuild these houses. The estimated cost at that time to repair the damage was over 18 million rand. We will shoot an interview with a case study in Sonderwater. This interview will demonstrate the suffering experienced by the residents as a result of this project. Also the councillors claim that no action has been taken to remedy the situation as recommended by the report. Greenfields - We will interview David Kham in Geenfields. He is one of the independent councillors serving in the municipality. David is also a former ANC councillor who was expelled, along with several other councillors in the area for voting with the opposition to remove ANC appointed mayor Maphetle Maphetle in 2013. (It's worth mentioning that Kham and Moolman spearheaded the Constitutional court application which resulted in by-election results in Tlokwe being set aside because of vote rigging). In Greenfields there are dozens of incomplete houses or foundations as a result of a contractor who began some of the construction, and then he ran off with the money and never completed the project.
metadata.Further information: There is also a new housing project that has tongues wagging in the area. The erection of about a thousand toilets on a vacant piece of land along the N12 in Extension 9. The municipality has simply erected toilets, not housing units or structures. The toilets were erected just before the elections. Councillors claim this project was not endorsed by the council and they have questioned the process. We get a response from Mr Mohlomi himself about the allegations levelled against him. We also chat to the mayor, Kgotso Khumalo too respond to the issue of Mohlomi's 'irregular appointment', as well as how to address some of the housing problems faced by the community. We also interview the current MEC for local government in the North West to find out how they will resolve the impasse. Especially if it seems the municipality is determined to retain him.
